scene1_screen1.text: It’s 5:58 AM, two minutes before the red light turns on. The studio buzzes with quiet urgency, like a live wire just waiting to spark. Makeup brushes are holstered. Mics are tested. And on set, two stars prepare for battle — with smiles.

scene1_screen2.text: Maria adjusts the collar of her silk blouse, her eyes flicking to her co-host. Jet-black eyeliner, flawless. He’s watching her. Of course he is.

scene1_screen3.text: Jed, sleeves rolled, hair perfect in that careless way that takes actual effort, leans back in his chair with the posture of a man who knows cameras love him. He smirks.

scene1_screen4.text: Don’t worry,  partner. I won’t make you look too bad today.

scene1_screen5.text: (flatly) You never make me look bad, Jed. If I look bad, that´s on me.

scene1_screen6.text: Their producer, Gloria, sweeps onto the set like a storm in heels. A tight black dress, a clipboard, and a gaze that lingers a second too long on Jed. Maria notices.

scene1_screen7.text: Alright, lovebirds. I’ve got news. Big news. The network is launching a prime-time concept — personal, edgy, unscripted. One of you is getting your own show.

scene1_screen8.text: A beat. Just long enough for reality to click in.

scene1_screen10.text: Only one. It’s not about chemistry anymore. It’s about commanding the screen — solo.

scene1_screen11.text: Jed raises an eyebrow, almost amused. Maria crosses her legs. Slowly.

scene1_screen12.text: This week, I want you both to pitch a segment — your concept, your vibe. Impress me. Starting… now.

scene1_screen13.text: She walks off, but not before brushing Jed’s shoulder with her fingertips. Barely. Maria tilts her head, filing that moment away like ammo.

scene1_screen14.text: (softly, to Maria) So… shall we dance?

opts.text: Turn up the heat with a flirt

scene1_choice1_option1_screen1.text: If this is a competition, may the best broadcaster win.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen2.text: She turns slightly toward the camera, shoulders squared, voice smooth as velvet.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen3.text: My show? It's about real mornings. The chaos, the confessions, the coffee-fueled truths we never say out loud.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Jed watches her, brows raised. His smirk fades, just slightly.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen6.text: Their eyes meet for a moment too long. The cameras may not be rolling yet, but the tension sure as hell is.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen1.text: You know what this audience wants, Jed?

scene1_choice1_option2_screen3.text: (smiling) A woman who can walk all over her co-host — in heels — and still make him say thank you.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen4.text: Jed lets out a low whistle. The stage lights don’t hide the glint in his eye.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen6.text: She leans in just enough to make it intimate — just enough to make it dangerous.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen7.text: Good. Keep that energy. You’ll need it… when I win.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Let’s skip the warm-up. I’m here to take the show — and leave no room for second place.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen2.text: Jed blinks, then grins slowly — that infuriating, infatuating grin of someone who loves a challenge.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen3.text: And here I thought this rivalry was just foreplay.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen4.text: Maria doesn’t blink. She steps closer, toe-to-toe now.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen5.text: Then you better make it count. Because I don’t play twice.

scene1_screen15.text: The red light turns on. The cameras roll. The teleprompter hums to life — but no one’s looking at it. Maria and Jed face the lens… but their focus is on each other.

scene1_screen16.text: The segment begins with scripted lines. It doesn’t stay there long.

scene1_screen17.text: They riff, interrupt, flirt, challenge — a perfectly choreographed tug-of-war. Sparks fly in high-def. The crew watches, stunned. Gloria watches… pleased.

scene1_screen18.text: But only Jed catches the moment Maria’s hand grazes his, just off-screen. And only Maria notices the way Jed leans slightly closer when the camera cuts to commercial.

scene1_screen19.text: Whatever this is, it’s not just about the job anymore. It’s a game of power. And it’s only just begun.

scene2_screen1.text: The cameras are off. The crew is gone. Only two microphones are still live — clipped to a silk blouse and an open collar.

scene2_screen2.text: Maria and Jed stand under the soft halo of light, rehearsing a “chemistry test” segment Gloria insisted they try. A couple on-screen. Conversational. Close. Too close.

scene2_screen3.text: So, I ask you how we balance work and… attraction.

scene2_screen4.text: (flipping her cue card) And I say, "We don't." We surrender to it.

scene2_screen5.text: Her voice is low, smooth, just above a whisper. Jed raises an eyebrow. The lines feel too real. The air is thick, like warm honey.

scene2_screen6.text: (stepping in) You sure this is a test, not a confession?

scene2_screen7.text: (smiling, dangerous) You tell me, Jed. You’re the one who can’t stop staring.

scene2_screen8.text: They move through the scene. On paper, it’s just dialogue. In practice, it’s a dance — eyes locking, fingers brushing when they reach for the same prop mug.

scene2_screen9.text: Maria sits on the edge of the mock sofa, legs crossed, skin glowing under studio amber. Jed paces, then joins her, a little too close. The scripted distance dissolves.

scene2_choice1.text: How do you take the scene forward?

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Jed turns toward her, knees brushing. His gaze doesn’t waver.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: What if the problem isn’t balancing work and attraction… But that we both secretly love the tension?

scene2_choice1_option1_screen3.text: Maria exhales — not quite a laugh, not quite surrender. His hand rests on the back of the couch. Not touching her. But surrounding her.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen4.text: We’re experts at pretending, Jed. But this part? You're not acting.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Jed shifts closer. Barely a breath between them now.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: Let’s drop the script. You and me. Right now.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: His hand grazes hers, then lingers. She doesn’t pull away. The heat builds — a wordless gravity.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: (flushed) If you kiss me, you better mean it.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen6.text: She blinks — caught. He’s never said that before. Her lips part. The moment balances on a whisper.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen2.text: Careful. We keep this up, and I might forget we’re competing.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen3.text: Careful. I might forget I’m supposed to let you win.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen4.text: She tosses a pillow at him. He catches it — and tosses it back, hitting her thigh. She lets out a surprised laugh. He laughs too, but his eyes linger — longer, warmer.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen5.text: You laugh like someone who doesn’t realize how breathtaking she is when she does.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen6.text: Silence. Just for a second. Her smile fades, replaced by something softer. Vulnerable.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen8.text: Neither are you. That’s why I like you.

scene2_screen10.text: The scene ends with no cue. No script left. Just them.

scene2_screen11.text: Maria stands. Jed watches her — like she’s something rare, wild, and barely within reach. She moves toward the exit, but then—

scene2_screen12.text: (low, without turning) You were serious. Back there. Weren’t you?

scene2_screen13.text: (quietly) I’ve been serious since the first time you stole the spotlight — and didn’t even notice.

scene2_screen14.text: She pauses. Breath caught. Then she leaves.

scene2_screen15.text: Jed stays behind, alone in the halo of warm studio light. Fingers brushing his own lips. Rehearsal’s over.

scene3_screen1.text: It starts with thunder. The kind that rattles sidewalks. The storm catches them both halfway down the street — soaked, breathless, laughing like it’s not the worst timing in the world.

scene3_screen2.text: They duck inside the first open door. The hostess blinks at their drenched clothes, then wordlessly gestures to the only free table.

scene3_screen3.text: Well. Not how I thought this night would end.

scene3_screen4.text: You say that like you didn’t enjoy getting caught in the rain with me.

scene3_screen5.text: She doesn’t answer. Just slides into her seat, arms crossed to warm herself. Jed shrugs off his jacket and drapes it over her chair.

scene3_screen6.text: You always pull the gentleman act when no one's watching?

scene3_screen8.text: A glass of red wine each. Soft jazz in the background. Her blouse clings lightly to her skin from the rain. His shirt collar is open, a little too relaxed.

scene3_screen9.text: Their laughter fades into a quieter rhythm. They fall into conversation like slipping into a familiar old sweater.

scene3_screen10.text: Do you remember our first day on camera?

scene3_screen11.text: Vividly. You nearly walked off set because someone called you “the pretty one.”

scene3_screen12.text: I was ready to walk. I didn’t spend six years in production school to be someone’s set dressing.

scene3_screen14.text: A beat. She looks at him — curious. Maybe even moved.

scene3_screen15.text: Why did you even start doing this? You don’t exactly scream “media darling.”

scene3_screen16.text: My mom was a radio host. Local news, tiny town. Every morning, she’d sit at this little desk with a mic and a smile and make people feel less alone. I wanted that. That connection.

scene3_screen18.text: (softly) Don’t tell anyone. It’ll ruin my reputation.

scene3_screen19.text: Maria smiles — not the usual smirk. Something warmer. More open.

scene3_screen20.text: Your turn. Why are you still here, Maria?

scene3_screen21.text: Because when it works — when you get a segment just right, and someone writes in saying it helped them — it feels like I’m not just screaming into the void.Like I exist. Fully.

scene3_screen22.text: He watches her like she’s just revealed a secret. Like, she is the secret.

scene3_choice1.text: How do you react to this moment?

opts.text: Step away from the heat, but stay honest

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: She leans in. No teasing. No dramatics. Just the soft press of lips that says: I’ve waited long enough.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen2.text: He exhales into it. Fingers brushing her cheek, anchoring her. It’s slow. Intentional. Real.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen3.text: When they part, his voice is barely a whisper.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen4.text: I’ve wanted that for so long, I forgot what it felt like not to.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Wow. You almost sound like someone with feelings.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen3.text: (gently) So prove me wrong. Or don’t.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen4.text: He reaches across the table. Touches her hand. No games. Just warmth.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen5.text: I’m not playing. Not with you.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Let’s not ruin it. This… this night is perfect. No expectations.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen2.text: But you feel it too, don’t you?

scene3_choice1_option3_screen3.text: Of course I do. That’s what makes it dangerous.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen4.text: Their hands stay on the table. Not touching. Not quite apart either. The pause between them is filled with everything unsaid — but known.

scene3_screen23.text: Outside, the rain shows no sign of stopping. But inside — they’ve found something rare.

scene3_screen25.text: I didn’t say it before… but I didn’t flirt back with Gloria because of professionalism. I didn’t flirt back… because she’s not you.

scene3_screen26.text: Maria looks down at her glass. Then back at him.

scene3_screen27.text: And you’re not who I thought you were, either.

scene3_screen28.text: He raises his glass slightly, like a toast.

scene3_screen31.text: The clink of glasses is soft. But the look that follows? Lightning.

scene4_screen1.text: Maria arrives first. She sits across from Gloria, spine straight, expression unreadable. She doesn’t ask questions. She doesn’t need to.

scene4_screen2.text: Jed enters moments later, his usual swagger dampened by something heavier — like anticipation pressed tight beneath his ribs.

scene4_screen3.text: Well. The numbers are in. The board has watched the tapes. And I’ve had… thoughts of my own.

scene4_screen4.text: She looks at Jed as she says it. Too long. Too warm. Maria sees it, of course. Doesn't flinch.

scene4_screen5.text: Jed… congratulations. You’re getting the solo show.

scene4_screen6.text: The words hit like the last chord of a song she almost knew by heart. Maria doesn’t blink. But she doesn't move, either.

scene4_screen7.text: Jed shifts. Doesn’t smile. Doesn’t celebrate.

scene4_screen9.text: (purring) Unless you’re planning to turn it down.

scene4_screen10.text: A long silence. Jed glances at Maria. Her jaw is tight, her eyes far away.

scene4_screen11.text: Anyway, we’ll get the announcement ready by next week. Maria, of course, you’ll stay on Morning Pulse — for now.

scene4_screen12.text: Maria rises. Not a word. She walks to the door, heels silent on the cold floor.

scene4_screen14.text: (slowly) You earned it. No need to explain.

scene4_screen15.text: Yes, there is. Because none of this means anything if it costs you.

opts.text: Take the lead role, but open your heart

scene4_choice1_option1_screen1.text: I want the show. I won’t lie about that.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen3.text: But I also want you. And I’m not going to pretend those two things can´t coexist. So here I am — asking you to be a part of this. Not behind me. Beside me.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen5.text: If we do this… It’s all in.

scene5_choice0_option1_screen8.text: The cameras are ready. The crew’s holding their breath. The show that everyone’s been whispering about finally goes live.

scene5_choice0_option1_screen9.text: And at its heart — two people who’ve been circling each other like oxygen to a flame. Now, it’s time.

scene5_choice0_option1_screen10.text: Jed steps into the frame alone. His voice is calm, polished — a man who knows this stage belongs to him. But then —

scene5_choice0_option1_screen11.text: Before we begin, I want to thank the person who helped shape every beat of this story. She's behind the scenes now — but never behind me.

scene5_choice0_option1_screen12.text: Then, the unexpected — he steps off camera. Walks into the booth. In front of everyone.

scene5_choice0_option1_screen13.text: (off mic, low) I'm done pretending. We work better when we're honest.

scene5_choice0_option1_screen14.text: He leans in and kisses her. Slow. Certain. On her terms, in front of the whole room. Gasps. Smiles. Cheers. Gloria looks furious. The interns look inspired.

scene5_choice0_option1_screen17.text: I was busy finding my mark.

scene5_choice0_option2_screen1.text: You should have gotten it. Your pitch was sharper. Cleaner. You deserved the lead.

scene5_choice0_option2_screen2.text: That’s not how this industry works.

scene5_choice0_option2_screen4.text: He turns, walks back into Gloria’s office. The door closes behind him.

scene5_choice0_option2_screen5.text: Maria stands frozen for a breath. Two. Then her phone buzzes. A message from Jed: “It’s yours now. I’ll stay in the shadows — if it means watching you light up the room.”

scene5_choice0_option2_screen6.text: She smiles. And this time, it reaches her eyes.

scene6_choice0_option2_screen8.text: The cameras are ready. The crew’s holding their breath. The show that everyone’s been whispering about finally goes live.

scene6_choice0_option2_screen9.text: And at its heart — two people who’ve been circling each other like oxygen to a flame. Now, it’s time.

scene6_choice0_option2_screen10.text: Maria walks onto the set, alone but radiant. Confident, composed. Her voice carries — not loud, but powerful.

scene6_choice0_option2_screen11.text: This show isn’t about headlines. It’s about stories. Real ones. So here’s mine: A man gave up his spotlight for mine. And in doing that, he made room for something better than ego. He made room for us.

scene6_choice0_option2_screen12.text: He watches her like he’s watching sunrise from a mountaintop — proud, a little in awe.

scene6_choice0_option2_screen13.text: After the final segment, she walks toward him, unclipping her mic. She doesn’t say anything. Just kisses him, arms sliding around his neck.

scene6_choice0_option2_screen14.text: He kisses her back like he’s been waiting for this cue all his life.

scene6_choice0_option3_screen3.text: I don’t care about the title. I care about what we create — together. The best segments we ever did were us. Not me. Not you. Us.

scene6_choice0_option3_screen4.text: You really think the network will go for it?

scene6_choice0_option3_screen5.text: I think they’ll go for anything that makes sparks. And we, Maria… We’re lightning.

scene6_choice0_option3_screen6.text: She considers. Then nods — once, sharp.

scene6_choice0_option3_screen7.text: Then let’s give them a storm. She approaches him sharply, passionately. He grabs her waist. The show has two leading roles left.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen9.text: The cameras are ready. The crew’s holding their breath. The show that everyone’s been whispering about finally goes live.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen10.text: And at its heart — two people who’ve been circling each other like oxygen to a flame. Now, it’s time.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen11.text: The show opens… on both of them. Maria and Jed, side by side at the table. Coffee mugs. Laughter. Energy you can’t fake.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen12.text: Welcome to Hearts at Work — the show where we talk shop, spill secrets, and ask: Can passion survive the nine-to-five?

scene7_choice0_option3_screen13.text: Spoiler: it can. Especially when the chemistry is completely, undeniably inappropriate.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen14.text: They banter, tease, laugh — but when the camera cuts to break, they’re still leaning close.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen15.text: Gloria watches from backstage, jaw clenched… but even she can’t deny the magic.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen16.text: As the “cut” sign flashes, Jed turns to Maria.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen18.text: Only if you kiss me after every take.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen19.text: He pulls her in. The kiss is bold, playful, familiar — like something they’ve been perfecting off camera.

scene7_choice0_option3_screen20.text: The crew pretends not to watch. But they do.

scene7_screen1.text: Whatever version of the story you followed…It ends the same way. Not with a fade to black — but with lips meeting, hearts racing, and something even stronger than rivalry:

scene7_screen2.text: Recognition. And the beginning of something real.
